# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 45 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 45 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_045_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 2 — Trust in God's Power to Keep the Commandments

**45:1** He said to me: "You know that you are a servant of God and serve in his dominion, and that his power is great and incomprehensible, and that he made all things and established them out of nothing, and that he alone contains all things and is himself contained by nothing.

**45:2** Have faith therefore in him and fear him; and in your fear of him, exercise self-control. Keep these things and cast away from yourself all evil desire, and clothe yourself with every good and holy desire. For if you keep these commandments, you shall live to God."

**45:3** "Lord," I said, "strengthen me, for I have many distractions from the world and from the devil and from those who rule the living and the dead and from powerful men. For there are many diversions that carry me away." "I know," he said, "but I will be with you and will deliver you from all of them. Only keep my commandments and you will not be given over to them. Trust in God and he will deliver you from them."

**45:4** "I do trust him, lord," I said. "But why do you not fear him as well?" he said, "seeing that you trust him." "Lord," I said, "your commandments are great and good and glorious and are able to save the soul of a man. But if a man should perceive that he is able to keep these commandments, he will keep them. But if the heart of a man has become very hardened toward God and there is great weakness in him, then he despairs and says in his heart: these things are too hard; I cannot keep them. His heart therefore becomes hardened and he forsakes the living God."

**45:5** "These thoughts are from the devil," he said, "who is hostile to your Lord. Do not let such thoughts enter your heart, and do not waver concerning these commandments, as though you were unable to keep them. Rather, call to mind him who is able to do all things and who accomplishes all things as he wills. Through his great power and his great glory he is able to fulfill all these things. Therefore put your trust in God and believe in him, and he will strengthen you."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and theological precision.*
